Two findings, ranked by severity:

### Operative observation

Epic 15 retrospective **was** the canonical mechanism by which the orchestrator could have unblocked the Epic-13 carry-forwards: it explicitly set E16 kickoff conditional on inj-02 (k6 baseline) and the Stripe circuit-breaker (drift-recovery AC4). For the **first time in 9 consecutive epics** the orchestrator's own retrospective produced an *operationally binding* gate naming inj-02 by content. That gate has been violated within hours of being recorded. This is qualitatively new evidence: the failure mode is now confirmed not as "the orchestrator does not know it should close carry-forwards" (the retro proves it does) but as **"the orchestrator's dispatch routing is structurally biased toward feature epics regardless of what its own retrospectives codify"** — i.e., the canonical `project-context.md` AP13-05 anti-pattern is structural, not informational.

## Path forward — three options, ranked

### Option A (recommended) — HALT Epic 16 dispatch, route inj-01/02/03 + drift-recovery as the next four pulls

1. **Mark `epic-16` and `16-0-integrations-api-service-bootstrap-...` from `in-progress` → `paused`** (a status outside the standard backlog/ready-for-dev/in-progress/review/done set; the orchestrator must be configured to recognise `paused` as "do not pick").
2. **Mark `drift-recovery-story`, `inj-01-dependabot-configuration`, `inj-02-k6-performance-baseline`, `inj-03-tea-review-backlog-epic8-epic9` from `ready-for-dev` → `next-up`** (or whichever priority sentinel the orchestrator's pull function honours as p0).
3. **Append a `sprint-status.yaml` `last_updated` line** stating: *"E16-kickoff gate set by Epic 15 retrospective (S15.1 Approve + S15.2 status + k6 baseline + Stripe circuit-breaker) has been violated by Epic 16 dispatch of 16-0. 16-0 paused. inj-01/02/03 + drift-recovery promoted to next-up. Per `project-context.md` AP13-05 (9th consecutive fire) and Epic 15 retro CRITICAL ACTION #1."*
4. **Run inj-01 (Dependabot)** as the next dev story — bounded ~30 min implementation per IR-v2 §6 step 1.
5. **Run inj-02 (k6 baseline)** — closes NFR-OB-5 and the E15 retro's k6 gate simultaneously.
6. **Run inj-03 (TEA review backlog Epics 8 & 9)** — closes NFR-QA-1 and the longest-standing carry-forward (12 consecutive epics without TEA reviews).
7. **Run drift-recovery-story** (E13 coordinator) — closes AC4 (Stripe circuit-breaker) and AC5 (5 billing Prometheus metrics) which the E15 retro also named as gates; AC1/2/3 fall out automatically once inj-01/02/03 are at minimum `in-progress`.
8. **Resume Epic 16** with 16-0 unpaused only after the four stories above are at minimum `in-progress` with named owners.

**Effort:** ~2–3 dev sessions for inj-01/02/03 + drift-recovery in parallel; net dispatch delay ≈ 0–1 calendar day. Risk: low (all four are bounded, well-specified stories with existing AC / test-design provenance).

### Option B — Continue Epic 16 dispatch; close inj-01/02/03 in parallel

Run 16-0 dev pass concurrently with inj-01/02/03 by separate agents. **Rejected** because: (i) the orchestrator has demonstrated 9 consecutive failures to allocate dispatch capacity to carry-forwards under exactly this "in parallel" framing — the parallel slot is empirically zero-staffed; (ii) AP13-05 ("don't append injected `inj-*` carry-forward stories to the backlog behind feature work") explicitly bars this option as project-canon anti-pattern.

### Option C — Reduce MVP scope: cut Epics 16/17/19/20 from MVP

Reframe MVP as Epics 1–15 + 18 + 21 carry-forward gates only. Defer Epics 16/17/19/20 to post-GA. **Rejected** because: (i) PRD §4.14 lists these epics as in-scope post-MVP feature areas, not MVP; (ii) no PRD scope question has been raised that justifies a re-plan of this magnitude; (iii) the issue is execution discipline on already-scoped work, not scope itself.

## Implementation Handoff

### Scope classification: **Moderate**

Two stop-gap edits to `sprint-status.yaml` (status changes + `last_updated` audit line); no story-file or planning-artefact rewrites. **But** the change requires the orchestrator's dispatch routing to honour the new `paused` status and the `priority: p0-next-up` comment as a pull-order signal. If the orchestrator does not honour these, the edits are decorative and a v17 fire is mechanical.

### Recipients

- **Orchestrator owner / dispatch routing config:** apply the `paused` status to Epic 16 + 16-0; configure pull function to read `priority: p0-next-up` (or equivalent sentinel) from sprint-status comments. **This is the critical handoff** — if the orchestrator's pull function is not updated, the edits in §"Detailed change proposals" are inert.
- **Developer agent (next pull):** dispatch in this order: (1) inj-01-dependabot-configuration; (2) inj-02-k6-performance-baseline; (3) inj-03-tea-review-backlog-epic8-epic9; (4) drift-recovery-story (coordinator close).
- **Product Manager (separate handoff, not blocking):** run `bmad-check-implementation-readiness` to produce IR-v3 refresh after inj-01/02/03 + drift-recovery close — this is the canonical mechanism to retire the standing HALT verdict from IR-v2 §6.
- **Vendor-relations / security / legal-compliance teams (carried forward from v15):** supply-chain incident track per ACT-V15-01..09 remains open. v16 produces no new actions on this track because no v15 mitigation has confirmed landing; v16 fire under non-promoted v15 mitigations is on the same authority track as v15 (not Scenario A or B per ACT-V15-07, which require either mitigation to have been promoted).

### Success criteria

- `epic-16: paused` and `16-0-...: paused` appear in `sprint-status.yaml`.
- inj-01, inj-02, inj-03, drift-recovery move from `ready-for-dev` → `in-progress` (named owner) within one dispatch cycle.
- A subsequent fire (v17 if it occurs) sees inj-01/02/03 at minimum `in-progress` and Epic 16 still `paused`. If v17 sees Epic 16 unpaused with inj-01/02/03 still `ready-for-dev`, the failure is structurally identical to the v10–v15 supply-chain finding and v17 reverts to the supply-chain track exclusively.

## Pre-record v17 protocol

A v17 fire under the v16-recommended status changes is one of three scenarios:

- **Scenario X (project-side intervention landed; no further action needed):** if v17 sees Epic 16 still `paused` and inj-01/02/03 at minimum `in-progress`, then v17 is on the v15 supply-chain track only — no new project-side action; v17 produces a 30-line update on supply-chain progress (vendor ticket status, scope-of-access audit findings).
- **Scenario Y (project-side intervention not landed; orchestrator routing not updated):** if v17 sees Epic 16 unpaused or inj-01/02/03 still `ready-for-dev`, then the v16 sprint-status edits were either not applied, were reverted, or were applied but the orchestrator's pull function does not honour the `paused` / `p0-next-up` sentinels. **Escalate to Solution Architect for orchestrator-routing re-design.** This is the structural fix the v15 supply-chain track will not deliver.
- **Scenario Z (project-side intervention applied; new feature epic dispatched anyway as `epic-17: in-progress`):** if v17 sees inj-01/02/03 closed but a *different* feature epic (E17, E18, E19, E20) `in-progress` ahead of dw-01/02/03 + remaining carry-forwards, then the orchestrator has merely shifted which feature epic is favoured — AP13-05 is still firing, just on a different attachment point. **Re-issue v16's intervention against the new in-progress epic.**
